title: Seborrheic dermatitis
intro: Seborrheic dermatitis is a common, harmless skin condition causing red, flaky, greasy-looking patches, especially on the scalp, face and chest. Dandruff is a mild form. It comes and goes, and responds well to medicated shampoos and creams, though it tends to return.

sections.heading: Where and how it appears
paragraphs: It affects areas with many oil glands: the scalp, eyebrows, sides of the nose, behind the ears, beard area and centre of the chest. Skin may be red with yellowish scales, and itchy or sore. In babies it appears as thick yellow scaly crusts on the scalp, called cradle cap, which is harmless and usually disappears within months.

sections.heading: Causes
paragraphs: The cause is a combination of skin oil, a yeast called Malassezia that normally lives on skin, and an individual inflammatory reaction. It is not caused by poor hygiene. Stress, tiredness, cold dry weather, certain illnesses such as Parkinson's disease and some medicines can trigger or worsen it.

sections.heading: Treating the scalp
paragraphs: Shampoos containing ketoconazole, selenium sulphide, zinc pyrithione or coal tar are used two to three times weekly until the condition settles, then less often, leaving the shampoo on for a few minutes before rinsing. Salicylic acid or oil can loosen thick scales. Cradle cap in babies may be softened with baby oil and gently brushed out.

sections.heading: Treating the face and body
paragraphs: Antifungal creams are applied once or twice daily. For redness and itching, a mild corticosteroid cream may be prescribed for short periods, as longer use thins the skin on the face. Because it tends to recur, maintenance treatment once or twice a week helps keep it away. See a doctor if the skin looks infected, is very widespread or does not respond.

sections.heading: Living with it
paragraphs: The condition is harmless and not contagious. Gentle skin care, avoiding harsh products and keeping to a simple routine help. Flare-ups often follow stress or poor sleep, so addressing these may reduce relapses.

examples.title: Using a shampoo
examples.text: Imagine your scalp is flaky and itchy. You could use an antifungal shampoo twice a week, leave it on for several minutes and continue until improvement before reducing use.

examples.title: Caring for a baby
examples.text: Suppose your baby has yellow crusts on the scalp. You might massage a little oil into the scalp, leave it for an hour and comb gently with a soft brush.
